# John 2 · The First Sign and the Cleansed Temple (KJV)
> Unit john-02 · John 2:1–25 · loop john-kjv-study v2.0 · DRAFT for human doctrine review

## 🧭 At a Glance
### 🧵 Golden Thread
Jesus reveals his glory by giving the best wine and by claiming to be the true temple, and he calls for faith that rests on him.

### 🌗 Life & Light Line
The chapter answers a feast run dry and worship turned into trade with the life of the Son who gives good wine and raises the temple of his body. It exposes faith that is only for show, and it gives the light of a Lord who knows what is in man.

### 🎯 Objectives
- Explain from John 2:11 why John calls the wine a sign that manifests the glory of Jesus.
- **Doing:** Name one place where you will obey the word of Jesus this week, as the servants did (John 2:5).

### 📋 Life & Light At-a-Glance
| | What is dead or dark | Where the source is, with verse | What I do about it today |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Life** | A celebration that has run dry | Jesus, who came to give life (John 10:10) | Bring my empty jar to him in prayer |
| **Light** | Faith that is only for show | Jesus, the light of the world (John 8:12) | Ask him to search my motives |

## 🏛️ Core Foundations
### ✝️ Christological Root
**Gospel Foundation:** Jesus himself grounds the chapter: "Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up." (John 2:19)

**The Bridge:** The temple of his body is the place where God meets men, so every doctrine of worship begins here.

**Canonical Echoes:** Jesus (John 2:19) → Promise (Malachi 3:1) → Doctrine (1 Corinthians 3:16) → Life (Ephesians 2:21)

**What Gets Lost:** Without this root, the cleansing becomes a lesson in church manners.

### ⚔️ Spiritual Warfare
**The Lie:** God can be managed by religious trade.

**The Truth:** Jesus says "make not my Father's house an house of merchandise" (John 2:16).

**The Battleground:** The motives of the heart.

**The Weapon:** The word of Christ, obeyed.

### 🌱 Life Pathway
**The Theft:** The wine runs out and the joy of the feast with it.

**The Source:** Jesus, who gives the good wine (John 2:10).

**The Channel:** Servants who fill the jars at his word carry the gift to others.

**The Abundance Guard:** Abundant life is fullness of life in Christ, not money or ease.

### 💡 Light Pathway
**The Darkness:** Belief that wants a show.

**The Source:** Jesus, who knows what is in man (John 2:25).

**The Lamp:** Scripture remembered, as the disciples remembered it (John 2:22).

**The Love Guard:** Light without love is glare.

### 🏺 Setting the Scene
Weddings in Galilee lasted for days, and the family of the groom was expected to keep the guests supplied. Running out of wine was a public shame for the host and his family. Six stone waterpots stood ready for the washings that the law and the traditions of the elders required, and each held two or three firkins. At Passover, Jerusalem filled with pilgrims who needed animals for sacrifice and temple coins for the tax, so traders set up in the court of the Gentiles. Herod had begun rebuilding the temple years before, and the work was still going on when Jesus spoke. John sets a quiet miracle in a village beside a loud confrontation in the capital, and both scenes point to the same question: who is this man, and where does God now meet his people? The narrator tells us more than the characters know, and he invites us to read the signs as they were meant to be read. The servants know where the wine came from; the ruler does not. The disciples understand the saying about the temple only after the resurrection.

### 🖍️ Read & Mark
**Marking key:** circle repeated words · underline commands · box names of God · double-underline promises

#### John 2:1–11 · The Wedding at Cana
**1** And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:

**2** And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.

**3** And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.

**4** Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.

**5** His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.

**6** And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece.

**7** Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.

**8** And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. And they bare it.

**9** When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom,

**10** And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now.

**11** This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

#### John 2:12–25 · The Temple and the Crowds
**12** After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: and they continued there not many days.

**13** And the Jews' passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem,

**14** And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:

**15** And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers' money, and overthrew the tables;

**16** And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise.

**17** And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.

**18** Then answered the Jews and said unto him, What sign shewest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?

**19** Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.

**20** Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?

**21** But he spake of the temple of his body.

**22** When therefore he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.

**23** Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, many believed in his name, when they saw the miracles which he did.

**24** But Jesus did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men,

**25** And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.

## 🟢 Tier 1 — Easy
### 📌 Core Concept
Jesus made water into wine to show who he is, and he cleaned the temple because God's house is for God.

### 📖 Key Verses
"His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it." (John 2:5) Obey Jesus.

"This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him." (John 2:11) Signs show his glory.

"Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up." (John 2:19) Jesus would rise from the dead.

### 🪞 Analogy
A porch light on at night tells you someone is home; the signs tell you God has come.

### 🔎 Diagnostic Check
- Do I do what Jesus says?
- Do I want signs more than I want Jesus?
- Is my worship for God or for show?
- Do I let Jesus search my heart?

### ✅ Action Step
Do one thing Jesus asks of you this week, right away.

### 🌗 Life and Light, Simply
Jesus gives life like new wine at a party. Jesus gives light by showing what is really in our hearts.

## 🟡 Tier 2 — Medium
### 📜 Walkthrough
#### John 2:1–5 · A Wedding and a Word
**Says:** John records the words "Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it" (John 2:5) in the flow of the scene.

**Means:** The words point past the moment to who Jesus is, as John's purpose says: "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ" (John 20:31).

**Asks:** Trust the word of Jesus and look for his glory.

#### John 2:6–10 · Water Made Wine
**Says:** John records the words "Fill the waterpots with water" (John 2:7) in the flow of the scene.

**Means:** The words point past the moment to who Jesus is, as John's purpose says: "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ" (John 20:31).

**Asks:** Trust the word of Jesus and look for his glory.

#### John 2:11–12 · The First Sign
**Says:** John records the words "manifested forth his glory" (John 2:11) in the flow of the scene.

**Means:** The words point past the moment to who Jesus is, as John's purpose says: "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ" (John 20:31).

**Asks:** Trust the word of Jesus and look for his glory.

#### John 2:13–17 · Zeal for the Father's House
**Says:** John records the words "make not my Father's house an house of merchandise" (John 2:16) in the flow of the scene.

**Means:** The words point past the moment to who Jesus is, as John's purpose says: "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ" (John 20:31).

**Asks:** Trust the word of Jesus and look for his glory.

#### John 2:18–22 · Destroy This Temple
**Says:** John records the words "But he spake of the temple of his body" (John 2:21) in the flow of the scene.

**Means:** The words point past the moment to who Jesus is, as John's purpose says: "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ" (John 20:31).

**Asks:** Trust the word of Jesus and look for his glory.

#### John 2:23–25 · He Knew What Was in Man
**Says:** John records the words "he knew what was in man" (John 2:25) in the flow of the scene.

**Means:** The words point past the moment to who Jesus is, as John's purpose says: "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ" (John 20:31).

**Asks:** Trust the word of Jesus and look for his glory.

### 🧨 Cultural Landmines and Misconceptions
Wine at a wedding was ordinary food, not a mark of excess.

## 🔴 Tier 3 — Expert
### 🏗️ Theological Framework
The chapter belongs to Christology and to the doctrine of worship.

### 📚 Scholarly Insights
J. C. Ryle, *Expository Thoughts on the Gospels*, reads the cleansing as a warning to churches.

### ⚔️ Debate Corner
Some hold one cleansing, others two; the Reformed reading lets each Gospel tell its own order.

**Pastoral Warning:** Don't let a dating debate eclipse the call to holy worship.

### 🔤 Original Language Deep Dive
The verb *episteusan* (G4100, John 2:11, V-AAI-3P) is the aorist of believing.

### 🚷 Preaching Mistakes to Avoid
- **Information without life:** teaching the customs of the wedding and never the Lord of it.
- **Heat without light:** anger at the money-changers without the cross of the true temple.
- Moralism: making the chapter a lesson in church manners.

## 📚 Doctrine
### Theology Proper · God Is Jealous for His House
**Proposition:** God Is Jealous for His House, as this chapter shows.

**Textual Anchor:** John writes "my Father's house" (John 2:16), and the claim rests on those words.

**Cross-References:** "Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the LORD of hosts." (Malachi 3:1); "And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves." (Mark 11:17)

**Errors Refuted:** This refutes the error that the chapter is only about a party or only about church buildings.

**Pastoral Fruit:** It humbles us before the Lord and moves us to worship him with holy lives.

### Christology · Jesus Manifests His Glory
**Proposition:** Jesus Manifests His Glory, as this chapter shows.

**Textual Anchor:** John writes "manifested forth his glory" (John 2:11), and the claim rests on those words.

**Cross-References:** "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth." (John 1:14); "But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;" (Hebrews 9:11)

**Errors Refuted:** This refutes the error that the chapter is only about a party or only about church buildings.

**Pastoral Fruit:** It humbles us before the Lord and moves us to worship him with holy lives.

### Anthropology & Sin · The Lord Knows the Heart
**Proposition:** The Lord Knows the Heart, as this chapter shows.

**Textual Anchor:** John writes "he knew what was in man" (John 2:25), and the claim rests on those words.

**Cross-References:** "The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?" (Jeremiah 17:9); "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;" (Romans 3:23)

**Errors Refuted:** This refutes the error that the chapter is only about a party or only about church buildings.

**Pastoral Fruit:** It humbles us before the Lord and moves us to worship him with holy lives.

### Soteriology & Grace · Faith Rests on the Person, Not the Show
**Proposition:** Faith Rests on the Person, Not the Show, as this chapter shows.

**Textual Anchor:** John writes "his disciples believed on him" (John 2:11), and the claim rests on those words.

**Cross-References:** "But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name." (John 20:31); "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life." (John 3:16)

**Errors Refuted:** This refutes the error that the chapter is only about a party or only about church buildings.

**Pastoral Fruit:** It humbles us before the Lord and moves us to worship him with holy lives.

### Eschatology · The Temple Raised in Three Days
**Proposition:** The Temple Raised in Three Days, as this chapter shows.

**Textual Anchor:** John writes "in three days I will raise it up" (John 2:19), and the claim rests on those words.

**Cross-References:** "And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it." (Revelation 21:22); "Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt." (Amos 9:13)

**Errors Refuted:** This refutes the error that the chapter is only about a party or only about church buildings.

**Pastoral Fruit:** It humbles us before the Lord and moves us to worship him with holy lives.

### Assumed Here
- **Pneumatology:** The chapter assumes the Spirit who later brings the disciples' memory to life (John 14:26).
- **Ecclesiology:** The chapter assumes a people who will be God's temple (1 Corinthians 3:16).
- **Christian Walk:** The chapter assumes obedience that does whatever he says (John 2:5).

## ⚖️ The Council's Hard Questions
### ❓ Question 1 · Was Jesus Rude to His Mother?
**Moderator:** How should we hear the word woman in John 2:4?

**Philologist:** It is a respectful address in the idiom of the day.

**Historian:** Mothers were honored in such families, and she was not rebuked.

**Resolution:** Jesus sets his hour above family pressure without dishonor (John 2:4).

### ❓ Question 2 · One Cleansing or Two?
**Literary Scholar:** John places the scene early for its meaning.

**Church Historian:** Many in the church have held two cleansings.

**Resolution:** Faithful readers differ; both views honor the text (John 2:13).

### ❓ Question 3 · Why Would Jesus Not Commit Himself?
**Theologian:** Faith in signs alone is not yet saving faith.

**Pastor:** The chapter warns us against a faith that wants a show.

**Teacher:** A group can see the difference between the disciples and the crowd.

**Resolution:** Jesus knows the heart and looks for faith in himself (John 2:24).

### 🔦 The Life & Light Audit
**Pastor:** A hearer who obeyed would bring an empty jar to Jesus and let him search the heart.

**Theologian:** Nothing here depends on the hearer's own power (John 15:5).

**Teacher:** A Level 1 participant could do both this week.

**Fix:** None was needed.

### 🐑 Shepherding Notes
The Light Planner's first row asks for something private; never make anyone read it aloud.

### 🎯 Teaching Angles
**For a Tier 1 Group:** Tell the wedding as a story and ask what Jesus showed.

**For a Tier 2 Group:** Trace the temple theme from Exodus to Revelation.

**Tough Question 1:** Did Jesus make alcohol? Yes; the text says wine, and the sign shows his glory.

**Tough Question 2:** Was Jesus angry? Yes, with a holy zeal for his Father's house.

**Tough Question 3:** Why did he not trust the crowd? Because he knew what was in man (John 2:25).
